name: Curd Rice
cuisine: South Indian (Tamil thayir sadam / Kannada mosaranna / Telugu daddojanam)

ingredients.name: Sona masuri rice (or ponni, or any short/medium-grain white rice), raw
ingredients.householdMeasure: ⅓ cup raw / about 1⅓ cups cooked

ingredients.name: Water (for cooking the rice; skip if using leftover rice)
Curd (dahi), plain, fresh and not sour
Milk (full-cream or toned), boiled and cooled
Sesame oil (gingelly oil/til oil; groundnut or coconut oil also used)

equipment: Pressure cooker (2–3 litre), only if cooking the rice fresh
Mixing bowl (the serving bowl is fine)
Potato masher, back of a steel ladle, or a large spoon, for mashing
Measuring cups and spoons (a normal teaspoon and a 200 ml tea cup are fine)
Microwave or small pan, only for warming leftover fridge rice

steps.title: Rinse the rice
steps.text: Put 60 g (⅓ cup) raw rice in the cooker base and rinse 2–3 times, rubbing gently, then drain.
steps.visualCue: The rinse water turns from milky to almost clear.
steps.cameraCheck: The rinsed rice in the cooker
steps.videoShot: Hand swirling the rice, cloudy water being tipped out.
steps.watchOut: Skipping the rinse gives gummy, pasty rice; if the water is still very cloudy, rinse once more.

steps.title: Pressure-cook the rice soft
steps.text: Add 180 ml (¾ cup) water, close the lid, cook on medium for 4 whistles, switch off and let the pressure drop on its own.
steps.tip: Curd rice needs softer rice than rice for dal, so use more water (3 parts to 1) and more whistles.
steps.visualCue: You hear 4 whistles; when you open the lid all water is absorbed and the grains are very soft and slightly broken.
steps.cameraCheck: The cooked rice in the open cooker
steps.videoShot: The lid lifting off steaming rice.
steps.watchOut: Firm, separate grains mean too little water or too few whistles, and they will not mash creamy; stir in 3 tbsp hot water and steam covered 3 min.

steps.title: Mash the rice
steps.text: While still hot, mash it with a masher or the back of a ladle.
steps.tip: Mash less if you like a grainy texture.
steps.visualCue: A soft, mostly smooth mash with some grains still visible.
steps.videoShot: The ladle pressing down on the rice.
steps.watchOut: Cold rice goes stiff and will not mash; if it has cooled, sprinkle a spoon of hot water and mash again.

steps.title: Cool the rice completely
steps.text: Spread the mash in the mixing bowl and leave it.
steps.tip: This is the most important step.
steps.visualCue: No steam rises; the middle of the rice feels at room temperature to a fingertip.
steps.cameraCheck: The cooled rice in the bowl
steps.videoShot: A finger touching the middle of the rice.
steps.watchOut: Curd added to warm rice turns thin and sour and kills the live cultures; if you are short of time, spread the rice thin and fan it for 5 min.

steps.title: Chop the chilli, ginger and coriander
steps.text: Finely chop ½–1 green chilli (3 g), ½ tsp ginger (3 g) and 2 tsp coriander (2 g). Break the dried red chilli in two.
steps.visualCue: Small, even pieces that will not be a big bite of raw chilli.
steps.cameraCheck: Chopped chilli, ginger and coriander on the board
steps.watchOut: Large chunks of green chilli give sudden heat in one spoonful; chop finer.

steps.title: Add the salt and curd
steps.text: Add ¼ tsp salt and 150 g (⅔ cup) curd to the cooled rice.
steps.visualCue: A white mound of curd sitting on the rice.
steps.cameraCheck: The curd in the bowl before mixing
steps.videoShot: The curd being spooned onto the rice.
steps.watchOut: Very sour curd makes the whole bowl sour; if it smells sharp, use 120 g curd and a little more milk.

steps.title: Mix in the curd
steps.text: Stir until rice and curd are fully combined.
steps.visualCue: Creamy, evenly white rice with no dry lumps.
steps.videoShot: The spoon folding curd through the rice.
steps.watchOut: Dry white lumps of rice inside mean it is under-mixed; press them against the bowl wall and stir again.

steps.title: Loosen with milk
steps.text: Add 40 ml (2½ tbsp) cooled milk and stir.
steps.tip: Make it a little looser than you want to eat it, because it thickens. Milk also slows souring, so lunchboxes get extra.
steps.visualCue: A soft, loose texture that drops slowly off the spoon, like thick porridge.
steps.cameraCheck: A spoonful dropping back into the bowl
steps.videoShot: Milk pouring in, spoon lifting loosened rice.
steps.watchOut: A stiff, pasty bowl will set harder as it stands; add 1 more tbsp milk. A runny bowl needs 1 tbsp more mashed rice.

steps.title: Set out the tempering
steps.text: Put mustard seeds (¼ tsp) and urad dal (½ tsp) in a small bowl. Keep red chilli, green chilli, ginger, curry leaves and hing next to the stove.
steps.tip: Pat curry leaves dry; wet leaves spit hard in hot oil.
steps.cameraCheck: The bowl of mustard seeds and urad dal with curry leaves beside it
steps.videoShot: Overhead shot of the tempering items by the stove.
steps.watchOut: Searching for an item mid-tempering burns the dal in seconds; have it all ready first.

steps.title: Heat the oil
steps.text: Put the tadka pan on medium heat with 1 tsp (5 ml) oil.
steps.visualCue: The oil shimmers and flows thinly when tilted.
steps.videoShot: Oil swirling in the small pan.
steps.watchOut: Smoking oil tastes bitter; if it smokes, switch off for 20 sec and start over with fresh oil.

steps.title: Crackle the mustard seeds
steps.text: Add the mustard seeds and urad dal.
steps.visualCue: The seeds pop and crackle within 10 seconds.
steps.cameraCheck: Seeds and dal in the oil
steps.videoShot: Mustard seeds jumping in the oil.
steps.watchOut: Seeds that do not pop mean the oil is too cold and give a raw taste; wait a few more seconds. Seeds can jump, so hold a lid over the pan.

steps.title: Fry the urad dal golden
steps.visualCue: The dal turns light golden and smells toasty.
steps.cameraCheck: The golden dal in the pan
steps.videoShot: Dal changing from creamy white to golden.
steps.watchOut: Dark-brown dal tastes bitter; lower the heat as soon as it colours quickly, and start again if it turns dark.

steps.title: Add the chillies, ginger and curry leaves
steps.text: Add the red chilli, green chilli, ginger and curry leaves; stir.
steps.visualCue: Curry leaves turn crisp and bright green; the ginger smells sharp.
steps.cameraCheck: The tempering with curry leaves in the pan
steps.videoShot: Curry leaves hitting the oil and spluttering.
steps.watchOut: Browned ginger or leaves taste burnt; move quickly to the next step.

steps.title: Add the hing and switch off
steps.text: Add a small pinch of hing, stir once, switch off the flame, and let the tempering stand 30–60 sec.
steps.tip: A short rest stops the very hot oil from shocking the curd.
steps.visualCue: The hing smell blooms at once and the spluttering stops.
steps.cameraCheck: The finished tempering in the pan
steps.videoShot: The pinch of hing dropping in, flame turning off.
steps.watchOut: Too much hing makes the whole bowl bitter; a small pinch (0.1 g) is enough.

steps.title: Pour the tempering over the curd rice
steps.text: Tip the tempering, oil and all, over the rice and stir it in.
steps.visualCue: A short sizzle, then the rice is flecked with black mustard seeds, golden dal and green curry leaves.
steps.cameraCheck: The tempering on the rice before stirring
steps.videoShot: The tempering sizzling onto the white rice.
steps.watchOut: Very hot oil can thin and split the curd (thin, watery bowl with whey on the side); let the pan rest first, and stir in a spoon of milk to rescue.

steps.title: Add the coriander and taste
steps.text: Stir in the coriander. Taste; add a pinch of salt or a little milk if needed.
steps.visualCue: Creamy white rice with green flecks; it smells of curry leaves, hing and ginger.
steps.cameraCheck: A spoonful of finished curd rice
steps.videoShot: Coriander going in and a spoon lifting some rice.
steps.watchOut: A flat taste means it needs salt; add a pinch at a time as the rice will take more than you expect.

steps.title: Rest, then serve
steps.text: Leave for 2–3 min (or chill 30 min in summer). Serve at room temperature or cool.
steps.visualCue: The rice has thickened slightly and looks glossy.
steps.videoShot: The bowl set down beside a spoon of pickle.
steps.watchOut: If it has gone stiff, loosen with 1–2 tbsp milk before serving.

reasons: no frying, only 1 tsp oil, and curd adds protein, calcium and live cultures when the rice is cooled first. It is cooling and easy to digest. Points come off for mostly white rice (high glycaemic load, fibre about 2 g), few vegetables, modest protein (about 12 g) and sodium of about 680 mg. Restaurant bowls may add cream, more salt or ghee and cashews, with unknown portions.

researchRating.basis: curd rice is the classic South Indian comfort food and traditional last course; a national chain (Madras Curd Rice Company) is built around it. Recipe ratings re-checked this cycle remain very high on large samples (Hebbar's Kitchen daddojanam 5/5 from 255 votes; temple-style thayir sadam 4.99/5 from 71 votes). Small deduction because it is seen as plain, everyday food and diners grumble at paying ₹200 or more for it on delivery apps.

storage: Best eaten the same day; it keeps souring. Refrigerate within 1–2 hours and eat within 1 day. Do not freeze (the curd splits). Do not reheat; eat from the fridge or stand 10 min and stir in 1–2 tbsp milk. For lunchboxes, use extra milk and a little less curd, since whey can separate when packed and left for hours (Hebbar's tip).
leftoverRemix: Curd rice paniyaram. Mix 1 cup leftover curd rice with 2 tbsp rice flour (or fine rava), 1 tbsp chopped onion and a pinch of salt into a thick batter. Cook spoonfuls in a greased paniyaram pan on medium-low with ½ tsp oil in total, 3–4 min per side, until golden. Serve with coconut chutney.
burnOff: about 5.7 km of running (400 ÷ 70 kcal/km, 70 kg adult), or about 8 km of brisk walking (about 1 hr 35 min at 5 km/h, about 50 kcal/km) (est.).

navratri.reason: rice is a grain; use samak rice (barnyard millet) and sendha namak, skip urad dal, hing and mustard (assumed the common rule set that avoids grains and table salt)

ekadashi.reason: rice is a grain and is avoided on Ekadashi under the common rule set

jain.reason: drop the fresh ginger (use sonth or skip); everything else is allowed

ramadan.reason: light, cooling and easy to digest; the curd gives protein and calcium for sehri, and it is gentle on an empty stomach at iftar

jain.reason: skip the fresh ginger (a root); use a pinch of dry ginger powder (sonth) or leave it out. Onion, garlic and potato are not in the recipe.

vegan.reason: use unsweetened coconut or soy yoghurt for the curd and plant milk for the milk; oil is already plant-based.

pescatarian.reason: vegetarian, no meat; dairy is allowed

sattvik.reason: no onion or garlic in the recipe; hing is used as the savoury note

glutenFree.reason: most hing sold in India is compounded with wheat flour; use a gluten-free hing or skip it

dairyFree.reason: curd and milk are the dish; use coconut or soy yoghurt and plant milk (see the Vegan variant)
